rows.reason: The depolarization mechanism through voltage-gated sodium channels is beyond the stimulus–response overview. The new pathway lesson does not test ion flux.
This synthesis combines resting potential, action-potential phases and saltatory conduction. No introduction-class lesson retrieves the whole sequence.
The inhibitory GABA or glycine receptor mechanism is different from the new general chemical-synapse retrieval. The question also conflates inhibition with obligatory hyperpolarization.
The old synthesis spans molecular release, postsynaptic integration and neurotoxins. The introductory receptor model keeps only the general mechanism.
Both cards ask the single retrieval of water as the source of the oxygen released during photosynthesis, independent of the reaction pathway.
The original asks for light reactions, electron transport and the Calvin cycle. The successor lesson compares only overall balances.
Identifying the final electron acceptor at mitochondrial complex IV is more specific than explaining glucose oxidation or oxygen use in the net reaction.
The original covers four aerobic stages and a numerical ATP yield. The introductory card asks about ATP–ADP coupling without transferring mastery of the pathways.
